title: Trade for catch-up: examining how global value chains participation affects productive efficiency
summary: Earlier studies of trade-driven catch-up overlooked global value chain participation as a way to speed up efficiency gains. The paper finds that GVC participation helps technology-lagging countries become more efficient and close the gap to the frontier.
keyFindings: GVC participation helps technology-lagging countries close the efficiency gap to the global frontier.
Gains are larger with more human capital, deeper financial markets and stable macroeconomic conditions.
Gains are larger for countries specialised in downstream activities.
methods: Data envelopment analysis of efficiency relative to the global frontier, regressed on GVC participation with panel fixed effects, difference-GMM, Tobit and fractional response models.
